items.markdown:
![Thai Shrimp Paste Dip - Nam Prik Gapi - Hot Thai Kitchen](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07281238-1672-0139-0000-221455e234da:4)
**Nam prik kapi** (น้ำพริกกะปิ) is `a classic, punchy Thai dipping sauce made by pounding fermented shrimp paste with chilies, garlic, lime juice, and palm sugar` . It is a quintessential staple in Thai cuisine, known for its bold balance of spicy, sour, salty, and funky umami flavors.[[1]](https://hungryinthailand.com/nam-prik-kapi/)[[2]](https://www.facebook.com/HotThaiKitchen/videos/funky-umami-shrimp-paste-dip-nam-prik-gapi-%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%B3%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%9E%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B4%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%B4/1460096048249791/)

How It's Served

This relish-like dip is rarely eaten on its own; it is designed to complement relatively bland or rich foods. You will almost always find it served on a platter alongside:[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_phrik) [[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_phrik)[[2]](https://www.eatingthaifood.com/thai-nam-prik-kapi-recipe/)

- **Fresh or steamed vegetables:** Such as cucumber, cabbage, long beans, and eggplant.
- **Fried mackerel (*pla too*):** A small, savory Asian mackerel.
- ***Kai jeow cha om*:** A fluffy Thai omelet made with pungent acacia leaves.
- **Steamed sticky or jasmine rice:** To anchor the meal.[](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5AFFqe1Htzg&t=165) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5AFFqe1Htzg&t=165)[[2]](https://www.facebook.com/HotThaiKitchen/videos/funky-umami-shrimp-paste-dip-nam-prik-gapi-%E0%B8%99%E0%B8%B3%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%9E%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B4%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%81%E0%B8%B0%E0%B8%9B%E0%B8%B4/1460096048249791/)[[3]](https://www.facebook.com/groups/646957562780857/posts/1047628866047056/)

How It's Made Authentic preparation requires a mortar and pestle to lightly crush and combine the ingredients into a coarse paste rather than a smooth, uniform sauce.[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nam_phrik) 

- **Shrimp Paste (*Kapi*):** Fermented krill that is often lightly toasted over a flame to bring out its fragrant, smoky umami notes.
- **Aromatics:** Pounded Thai bird's eye chilies (for intense heat), garlic, and sometimes shallots.
- **Seasoning:** Freshly squeezed lime juice and palm sugar balance the intense saltiness of the paste.
- **Add-ins:** Dried shrimp are sometimes added for extra meatiness and texture, along with a few pea eggplants (*makhua puang*).[](https://www.eatingthaifood.com/thai-nam-prik-kapi-recipe/) [[1]](https://www.eatingthaifood.com/thai-nam-prik-kapi-recipe/)[[2]](https://support.google.com/knowledgepanel/answer/9787176)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y4YKSgkWdTA)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=azwc6Ns1KNo)[[5]](https://hot-thai-kitchen.com/shrimp-paste-dip/)
